---
title: "Crop cover"
lang: en
---

Forty-nine variables give the **share of each parcel** in seven land-cover groups, for each of the seven years 2019–2025. Scripts: `06-crop.R` (2019–2024) and `07-crop-2025.R` (2025).

## Variables

Variables are named `crop_<group>_<year>`. Each is a share from 0 to 1 of the parcel's classified (non-NoData) area. For a parcel and a year, the seven shares sum to 1.

| Group | Variables (2019 … 2025) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `built` | `crop_built_2019` … `crop_built_2025` | Artificial surfaces: buildings, roads, towns |
| `ag` | `crop_ag_2019` … `crop_ag_2025` | Cropland: all crop classes, including vineyards and nut trees |
| `forest` | `crop_forest_2019` … `crop_forest_2025` | Forest, including damaged forest |
| `grass` | `crop_grass_2019` … `crop_grass_2025` | Grassland, gardens and parks, low trees |
| `bare` | `crop_bare_2019` … `crop_bare_2025` | Bare land, not cultivated land |
| `water` | `crop_water_2019` … `crop_water_2025` | Water and wetland |
| `other` | `crop_other_2019` … `crop_other_2025` | Any code not in the table below |

The full list of 49 names is on the [Output](output.qmd) page. All rows have `source = "observed"`.

## Crop code table

The class codes of the maps changed over the years. Categories are matched by **label**, not by code: for example, "Not cultivated" is 22 in 2022 and 20 from 2023, and "Damaged forest" is 23 in 2022 and 25 from 2024. No code means two unrelated things in different years, so **one table of codes serves every year**.

| Group | Category | 2019 | 2020 | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 summer | 2025 winter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| built | Artificial | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | 1 | |
| ag | Wheat | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | 2 | |
| ag | Winter cereal | | | | | | | | 2 |
| ag | Rapeseed | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 | |
| ag | Winter rapeseed | | | | | | | | 3 |

| ag | Maize | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | 5 | |
| ag | Sugar beet | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | 6 | |
| ag | Sunflower | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | 7 | |
| ag | Soybeans | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 | |
| ag | Other crops | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | 9 | |
| ag | Barley | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 | 15 (Winter barley) | |
| ag | Peas | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 | 16 | |
| ag | Alfalfa | 17 | 17 | 17 | 17 | 17 | 17 | 17 | |
| ag | Grape | 19 | 19 | 19 | 19 | 19 | 19 | 19 | |
| ag | Potatoes | | | | 21 | 21 | 21 | 21 | |
| ag | Tomato | | | | | | | 24 | |
| ag | Nut trees | | | | | | | 26 | |
| ag | Other cereal | | | | | | | 27 | |
| forest | Forest | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | 10 | |

| grass | Gardens, parks / Low trees | 18 | 18 | 18 | 18 | | 18 | 18 (Low trees) | |
| bare | Bare land | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | 12 | |

| (NoData) | 0 | NA | NA | NA | NA | NA | NA | NA | NA |

In `00-setup.R`, this is one `tribble()`:

```r
crop_groups <- tribble(
  ~code, ~group,
  1,  "built",
  2,  "ag",  3,  "ag",  4,  "ag",  5,  "ag",  6,  "ag",  7,  "ag",  8,  "ag",  9,  "ag",
  15, "ag",  16, "ag",  17, "ag",  19, "ag",  21, "ag",  24, "ag",  26, "ag",  27, "ag",
  10, "forest", 23, "forest", 25, "forest",
  11, "grass",  18, "grass",
  12, "bare",   20, "bare",   22, "bare",
  13, "water",  14, "water"
)
```

## Method, 2019–2024

`06-crop.R` has one explicit block per year, with the year written out in full. For each year:

1. `rast(crop_2019)` is read and `NAflag(r) <- 0` is set: code 0 is NoData (background) in every year;
2. the parcels are transformed to the map's CRS (EPSG:32636); the 10 m map is never reprojected;
3. `exact_extract(r, p, "frac")` gives, for each parcel, the share of its classified area in each code. Each 10 m pixel is weighted by the share of it inside the parcel, and NoData pixels are left out of the total;
4. the codes are joined to `crop_groups`; codes not in the table become `"other"`;
5. shares are summed by group, and missing groups are completed with 0, so every parcel has all 7 groups.

A parcel entirely on NoData would get 0 for every group; the script prints how many there are each year.

## The 2025 rule: winter over summer

For 2025 there are two maps: a summer map (all classes) and a winter map that marks only **winter cereal (2)** and **winter rapeseed (3)**. Winter crops are harvested by midsummer, so the summer map can miss them. `07-crop-2025.R` combines the two:

- inside each parcel, a pixel takes the **winter code** where the winter map is 2 or 3, and the **summer code** otherwise;
- winter non-crop classes and winter NoData never overwrite the summer map;
- the rule is applied per pixel inside the parcels, never on the whole raster.

Both winter codes belong to `ag`, so the rule moves area from other groups into `ag`. In this run it changes the group shares of **135 parcels**.

The two maps have the same size but their origins differ by about 2 m (less than a quarter of a pixel). After a guard check (same dimensions, origins less than 5 m apart), the winter map is given the summer map's extent with `ext(winter) <- ext(summer)`. That matches each winter pixel to its nearest summer pixel, without resampling. `exact_extract()` then returns both values for every pixel in the parcel, with its coverage fraction, and the shares are computed from the combined code.

## Summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-crop-by-year
#| tbl-cap: "Mean share of each group over the 1,000 parcels, by year. From `output/tables/crop_by_year.csv`."
crop_by_year <- read.csv("../../output/tables/crop_by_year.csv")
crop_mean <- reshape(crop_by_year[, c("year", "group", "mean_share")],
                     idvar = "group", timevar = "year", direction = "wide")
names(crop_mean) <- c("Group", "2019", "2020", "2021", "2022", "2023", "2024", "2025")
knitr::kable(crop_mean, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-crop-ag
#| tbl-cap: "Share of parcels where cropland (`crop_ag`) covers more than half of the parcel, by year."
crop_ag <- crop_by_year[crop_by_year$group == "ag", c("year", "share_parcels_above_half")]
names(crop_ag) <- c("Year", "Share of parcels with crop_ag > 0.5")
knitr::kable(crop_ag, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

The `nodata` parcels were placed on towns, rivers and the reservoir, so the built and water shares are much higher than in a typical farm parcel.
